`EnergyModelWindowConfigMutation` is the config state lane of `s.energy.model`'s ✏️editor/🎭️modes/✏️edit/🪟️windows/🧊️model/🎚️config surface: it holds the 3d model window's camera pose (position, target, zoom). This is this repository's own editor state record, not a published format, so no third party implements it. What is under test is that each kind (`set-camera`) changes exactly its own part of `EnergyModelWindowConfig`, that a kind declaring `no-op` leaves a record that already holds its value untouched with a warned `mutation.no-op`, and that every kind's computed inverse, read off the pre-mutation record, restores it exactly. 🔮️ Test-only references of the quiz product (Protocol v2). Every case under ../🧪️tests names one of these oracles; the TypeScript twin (@semio-tech/quiz) and the Rust twin (semio-framework-quiz) are the subjects and are additionally held to each other. The Python references live inside the case adapters (🧪️tests/*/🐍️.py) and are written from the design text only. Shared vectors under ../🧫️fixtures are generated from those same adapters, so a committed vector and its oracle can never disagree; the generation command is stated in every feature.

Judges the home grid of @semio-tech/quiz-react inside its unit suite `🧪️tests/🏠️home-grid` (vitest, devDependency of the react package): lightningcss — the CSS engine Tailwind itself runs the site's styles through — parses the renderer's stylesheet into media queries, grid track lists and variables, and the tracks the card layer takes at 320 to 1440 px (the overview's `--quiz-home-columns`/`--quiz-home-rows` wherever the cards stand on the grid, the strip's own equal tracks where the learner swipes through it below tablets, no gap or padding between tracks, the spacing inside `.quiz-home-cell`) and the breakpoints themselves must equal the shared vectors and the design system's `UI_MOBILE_MAX_WIDTH_PX` / `UI_TABLET_MAX_WIDTH_PX`; it also parses the overview's own track lists into fr weights that must equal the shared weights of each layout (1 : 1.5 : 1 by 1 : 1.4 : 1 on desktops). jsdom lays nothing out and evaluates no media query (the width is emulated through `matchMedia`), so the stylesheet's own parse is the independent reading; the two-device walk in a real browser confirms the same grid. It judges the adaptive layout the same way inside `🧪️tests/📐️adaptive-layout`: its parse of every `@container` rule — the room a rule asks, how it compares the room's width with which length, and the class each rule inside starts with — must be exactly the tiers of the shared vectors (`🧫️fixtures/📐️adaptive-layout`: which part measures which room, from how many rem), every room must be declared a named inline-size container, and every folding table must fold by the one 36em query of its frame; what each width then looks like is held by the walk of the site at a phone's, a tablet's and two desktops' widths in a real browser.

One structured observation as `semio-framework-trace`'s `TraceRecord::to_json_line` writes it: one JSON object per line on the configured sink (`SEMIO_TRACE_SINK` = `stderr` | `stdout` | `none` | `file:<path>`), admitted by `SEMIO_TRACE_LEVEL`. `requestId` is the span id: the admission record of a long-lived span (a socket) and the record that ends it carry the same id. Absent identity fields are omitted, never written as null. The event vocabulary an operator may alert on is `⏱️trace/🧪️tests/🧫️fixtures/🛰️span-vocabulary/🔣️.json`.

The independent decimal oracle of `🧪️tests/🧪️number-facets` (staged-argument number facets) over `🧪️tests/🧫️fixtures/🧫️number-facets`: it recomputes every refusal's bound in display units (`value × displayFactor` to twelve significant digits) beside the shown unit.

Which bundle manifest selects which runner, and which argv a repo:// scope becomes, is this repository's own vocabulary — the bundle table, the entity-URI grammar and the narrowing order are defined nowhere outside semio, so no third-party library, CLI or standards tool can be a reference for them. Confidence comes instead from specification vectors frozen in 🧫️fixtures/🧭️detection-vectors.json and 🧫️fixtures/🗺️planning-vectors.json, each carrying the exact expected language and argv transcribed from the Go implementation this port reproduces, plus metamorphic laws asserted in the features (narrowing a scope never widens its plan; a filter only ever adds arguments; planning is idempotent).

Judges three claims of @semio-tech/pets-react inside its suites (vitest in jsdom, devDependency of the react package). In `🧪️tests/🪞️fixture-lifting` the copy of a lifted host element must be decoration like the pets: @testing-library/dom's accessibility tree must hold none of its nodes (`getRoles` empty, `isInaccessible` true for every node), whatever controls, links, labels and roles the original holds. In `🧪️tests/🫥️decorative-layer` the pet layer must be decoration (design §6.5): with a cast on stage, @testing-library/dom's accessibility tree — built on aria-query's role model — must hold no node of the layer (`getRoles` is empty for it, `isInaccessible` is true for the layer and every descendant) and a query for each of aria-query's concrete roles must find nothing in it. In `🧪️tests/📡️surface-survey` the default keep-outs must cover what a person can operate (design §6.3): every role the selector of controls names must be a concrete widget role by aria-query's superclass chains, and over a sample of native and ARIA elements the selector must match exactly those whose role — implicit by @testing-library/dom, or explicit — aria-query calls a widget. The geometry of the survey is held to shared vectors (`🧫️fixtures/📡️surface-survey`) computed by a second reading of the design written in Python from the design text (`generate_survey_vectors.py` of ticket 2026/10/02/QUIZ-PETS: tag and attribute tables instead of a selector engine, interval arithmetic) — a supplement, never third-party evidence; no library measures a page into surfaces and keep-outs by these rules. Frame pacing (`🧪️tests/⏲️frame-pacing`) runs on a hand-driven clock and on the fake clock of vitest itself.

Judges the learner's hand of @semio-tech/pets-react (`🔨️modules/🤏️grasp`, design-v2 §14.1, §17, §22) inside its suite `🧪️tests/🤏️pet-handling` (vitest in jsdom, devDependency of the react package). user-event plays the browser's side of a press as the Pointer Events and UI Events specifications describe it: a cancelled `pointerdown` suppresses the compatible `mousedown` and with it focus and the start of a text selection, but not the click, which goes to the nearest common ancestor of where the press began and ended; a press that is not cancelled focuses what it lands on and selects text as it moves; a label hands its click on to its control. Held against that model: a press on a pet with nothing interactive beneath it reaches no listener of the page (no `pointerdown`, `mousedown` or `click` on the element beneath or the document, no focus, no selection), while the same press beside the pet reaches all of them; a press on a button, a label or a host's grip under a pet is the control's (it is clicked, focused, checked); words beside the pets are selected by a drag and a selection holds the next press back from the pets; Escape calls a held pet off and is kept from the page, every other Escape and the keyboard's click pass; a tap with a finger is a press like a mouse's and its click is swallowed; a second finger is never a press of its own. The stage events the layer hands the core (pressed, the latest drag of a frame, released, cancelled, played, permitted, stirred, scrolled) are held by a fake core in the same suite; the walls of the survey by the shared vectors of `🧫️fixtures/📡️surface-survey` (see pets-react-aria-query).

🧭️ The argv grammar — subcommand selection stopping at the first operand, `--` ending flag parsing, `--help` short-circuiting at the command selected so far, a boolean flag never consuming the next token, a command with flag parsing disabled swallowing everything after its name, and the verbatim refusal messages — is this repository's own command framework, written in place of a third-party parser precisely so no external library appears in the runtime. A third-party argument parser would answer a DIFFERENT grammar, so comparing against one would test the wrong contract. The evidence is the vectors in 🧫️fixtures/🔣️argv-vectors.json, each stating either the whole projection or the verbatim message, read off the reference Go framework, plus the idempotence law.

🖨️ The three renderers project this repository's own event stream into this repository's own presentation vocabulary: an NDJSON body that is only the result payload, a human line built from entity ids minted by 🪪️identity, and a markdown list of `repo://` links. Nothing outside this checkout produces or reads those bytes. The evidence is the vectors in 🧫️fixtures/📡️event-streams.json, which state the exact stdout, stderr and exit code for every format including the coloured terminal case, plus two laws: no escape sequence survives a non-terminal render, and all three formats report the exit code the `done` event carried.

🧪️ Which runner a testable entity's tests belong to — `go test ./...` for a module, `cargo test` for a crate, `npx vitest run` for a vitest manifest, `uv run pytest` for a Python bundle — and in which order a list of operands announces them, is this repository's own scope algebra over its own bundle taxonomy. A third party could run the runners but could not decide the mapping, and running them would measure the runners rather than the verb. The evidence is one frozen filesystem snapshot and the vectors in 🧫️fixtures/🧪️test-verb-vectors.json, each stating the `Running: …` lines in order and the refusals, plus the determinism law.

The mapping from eight IDEs' native hook events onto one neutral event vocabulary is defined by this repository and by nothing else: the neutral slugs are ours, the tool-kind classification that decides which of them a `PreToolUse` becomes is ours, and each IDE's own documentation stops at the native name. No third-party library consumes any of it, and the IDEs themselves cannot be asked — they emit events, they do not adjudicate mappings, and driving eight editors from a test would put eight GUIs inside a test run. Confidence therefore comes from frozen specification vectors: `🧫️fixtures/🔀️native-events.json` pins the expected neutral event and parent hint beside every native one, written from the hook configurations this repository actually commits (`.claude/settings.json`, `.cursor/hooks.json`, `.windsurf/hooks.json`, `.kiro/agents/repo.json`), so an implementation must agree with the specification rather than with itself; the refusal vectors additionally pin that an unknown native name is an error and never a defaulted event. This decision covers no runtime mutation capability.

🌳️ Which category a record lands in, how a subgoal hangs under its goal, how a statute path becomes categories and how a territory lists its statutes are decisions this repository makes about its own artifacts. No third party produces or reads these trees, so no reference implementation exists to be had. The evidence is the record set and the expected outlines committed under `🧫️fixtures`, which restate the shape the Go original builds, plus two independently written implementations that must agree on them line for line. Both implementations additionally take their entity rendering and artifact ids through ports the fixture states, so a drift in 🪪️identity or the CLI renderers cannot silently repair a wrong tree.

The independent syntax-tree reading of every label site in `🧪️tests/🧪️mutation-history-gates`: the `schema mutation-labels` token gate and the tree-sitter-rust parse must give the same verdict on every corpus case of `🧪️tests/🧫️fixtures/🧫️mutation-labels`.

🔏️ Both implementations hand-roll SHA-256 — the Rust crate borrows the events crate's `Sha256`, the Go package uses `crypto/sha256` — and the checksum formula is frozen in 🧫️fixtures/🧬️g3-event-schema.json as text, not as code. Comparing the two implementations only to each other would prove that one reading of that sentence was transcribed twice. `node:crypto` reaches OpenSSL, an independent FIPS 180-4 implementation, and decides the envelope checksum and the canonical line from outside this repository.
